Comprehensive systems contribution addressing multiple practical bottlenecks: scalable distributed infrastructure supporting 1000+ parallel environments, LLM-automated API generation, and distributed training framework

Well-executed experimental methodology including meaningful ablations (API-GUI paradigm provides 134% improvement), reward/entropy analysis demonstrating training dynamics, and both successful and failed case studies

Incomplete technical justification: Three-stage training pipeline introduces many hyperparameters without sensitivity analysis; limited justification for specific pipeline choice; API automation success rate not reported; computational costs and resource requirements not thoroughly discussed

Missing critical ablations: contribution of BC stage alone, impact of each training phase in isolation, scalability analysis of parallel environments, sensitivity to key hyperparameters (clipping threshold, SFT frequency), and rule-based vs. learned reward comparison

Reproducibility challenges: code and models not publicly available, dependency on closed-source LLMs for BC stage, requires substantial computational resources, and limited evaluation scope (Ubuntu-only, small backbone models 9B-14B)

Limited scope and generalization: Ubuntu-only evaluation without evidence of transfer to Windows/macOS; no analysis of which task categories benefit from API-GUI; ~52% failure rate deserves rigorous investigation beyond high-level error categorization
